rationale: Large cohort studies (Sudnawa et al., 2026; Platzer et al., 2019) substantiate that individuals with MAPK8IP3 missense variants generally exhibit significantly more severe overall neurodevelopmental symptoms and higher penetrance of structural brain malformations (such as perisylvian polymicrogyria, hypoplasia of the corpus callosum, and cerebral/cerebellar atrophy) than individuals with truncating/LOF variants. However, this dichotomy is conflicted by recent reports demonstrating that heterozygous loss-of-function truncating variants can also present with severe global developmental delay, profound intellectual disability, and autism with marked intrafamilial variability (Yi et al., 2026), as well as functional evidence showing that missense variants localized within specific regions (e.g., the WD40/protein-interaction domain) phenocopy loss-of-function alleles and may themselves act via loss-of-function mechanisms (Crowder et al., 2026; Snead et al., 2022).

evidence.text: In a cohort of 32 individuals harboring heterozygous pathogenic MAPK8IP3 variants, individuals carrying missense variants (62.5%) were found to have significantly more severe overall symptoms compared to those with predicted loss-of-function variants (34.4%).

evidence.text: Evaluation of 13 unrelated individuals with de novo MAPK8IP3 variants demonstrated that major structural brain malformations (perisylvian polymicrogyria, cerebral or cerebellar atrophy, and hypoplasia of the corpus callosum) were consistent among individuals harboring recurrent de novo missense variants.

source.quote: Brain anomalies such as perisylvian polymicrogyria, cerebral or cerebellar atrophy, and hypoplasia of the corpus callosum were consistent among individuals harboring recurrent de novo missense variants.

evidence.text: Characterization of a familial canonical splice-site truncating variant (p.Gly877Valfs*36) demonstrated marked interindividual variability among 3 carriers, with one individual exhibiting global developmental delay, severe intellectual disability, and autism, showing that LOF variants are capable of causing severe clinical presentations.

source.quote: Notably, despite carrying an identical genotype, the three affected individuals exhibited marked interindividual variability in clinical severity, ranging from mild specific learning difficulties to global developmental delay with severe intellectual disability and autism.

evidence.text: Functional and phenotypic analyses in mouse and human models reveal that missense variants within the WD40/protein-interaction domain phenocopy truncating loss-of-function alleles, indicating that phenotypic severity is driven by domain-specific disruption rather than a blanket missense-versus-LOF distinction.

evidence.text: Five individuals with recurrent de novo missense variants (p.Arg578Cys and p.Arg1146Cys) consistently manifested core neurodevelopmental phenotypes of spastic diplegia, intellectual disability, cerebral atrophy, and hypoplasia of the corpus callosum.

source.title: Recurrent de novo MAPK8IP3 variants cause neurological phenotypes
source.quote: We identified 5 individuals from four families with recurrent de novo variants c.1732C>T (p.Arg578Cys) and c.3436C>T (p.Arg1146Cys) in MAPK8IP3. The core phenotype includes spastic diplegia, intellectual disability, cerebral atrophy, and corpus callosum hypoplasia.

conflicts: Yi et al. (2026) report that an inherited loss-of-function splice-site variant (p.Gly877Valfs*36) results in global developmental delay, severe intellectual disability, and autism, refuting the generalization that LOF variants are consistently mild or lack severe neurodevelopmental impact.

Crowder et al. (2026) demonstrate that missense variants within the WD40 domain phenocopy truncating LOF alleles in vivo, showing that clinical severity is specific to protein domains rather than segregating categorically into missense vs. LOF.

Snead et al. (2022) indicate that pathogenic missense variants act mechanistically as loss-of-function mutations in neuronal endocytosis assays, challenging a distinct dominant-negative mechanism as the sole driver of heightened severity.

new_directions.question_text: Do specific missense variants in MAPK8IP3 exert dominant-negative or toxic gain-of-function effects on retrograde axonal transport compared to pure haploinsufficiency?
new_directions.rationale: Investigating whether recurrent missense variants disrupt dynein/kinesin binding differently from truncating nonsense/frameshift variants will clarify the mechanistic origin of severe cortical dysgyria versus variable intellectual disability.

new_directions.question_text: What is the penetrance of cortical malformations (such as polymicrogyria) across a harmonized multicenter registry comparing truncating vs. non-WD40 missense MAPK8IP3 variants?
new_directions.rationale: Existing cohorts are small (n=13 to 32); a systematic neuroimaging review across a larger international cohort is required to definitively quantify brain anomaly penetrance by variant class.
